32. The menopause usually occurs between the ages of 45 and 55, but it can happen much
earlier, and can typically last around four years. There is also a period of hormonal change
leading up to the menopause known as the perimenopause. Physical and mental symptoms
can include hot flushes, urinary problems, heavy periods, sleep disturbance, fatigue,
headaches, lack of concentration, memory problems, palpitations, anxiety and mood swings.

33. The Women and Equalities Committee reported that menopause symptoms can be
exacerbated by work and stress caused by the work environment, including inability to
control ventilation, temperature, light and noise, lack of access to toilets and having to wear
synthetic or restrictive workwear. Their survey revealed that some women felt it necessary to
cut back their hours, or miss out on or forego promotion or similar advancement
opportunities, or felt forced to leave the workplace or were dismissed for reasons they
believe were connected with menopause symptoms.
